sentences.zh: 其实它不太像“深谷乱飞”，因为“深谷乱飞”，你知道的，你可以看到它的影像资料。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Whereas this, it's difficult to get a handle on.
sentences.zh: 而这个，却很难让人捉摸。

sentences.en: So it's, it's, there's a lot of myth here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有很多神话色彩。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But the myth in itself is very powerful and it's important.
sentences.zh: 但神话本身非常强大，而且很重要。

sentences.en: So I think that's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这没问题。

sentences.en: So let's come back to that in a second, but now just give us an overview.
sentences.zh: 那我们一会儿再回过头来谈这个，现在先给我们做一个概述。

sentences.en: Who are the Spartans?
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人是谁？

sentences.en: What's the story?
sentences.zh: 故事是怎样的？

sentences.en: Why do they end?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会走向终结？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Sparta is, it's, it's, it's girt on both side by great mountain ranges.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达的四周都被巨大的山脉环绕。

sentences.en: It's got the sea to the south.
sentences.zh: 南面临海。

sentences.en: It's got kind of dark hills to the north.
sentences.zh: 北部则有些阴暗的山丘。

sentences.en: So it's very naturally well fortified.
sentences.zh: 所以它天然就是一个防御工事极佳的地方。

sentences.en: So it's, it's ideally suited basically to be a military power.
sentences.zh: 因此它基本上非常适合成为一个军事强国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In, in, in mythology, it's chiefly famous as the home of Helen, who, who marries Menelaus, the king of Sparta at that generation after the Trojan war.
sentences.zh: 在神话中，它主要以海伦的故乡而闻名，海伦在特洛伊战争之后的那一代人中，嫁给了斯巴达国王墨涅拉俄斯。

sentences.en: So it gets burnt.
sentences.zh: 所以它被烧毁了。

sentences.en: New people come.
sentences.zh: 新的人们到来。

sentences.en: These are the people who claim to be the Spartans supposedly.
sentences.zh: 这些人据称就是自称为斯巴达人的人。

sentences.en: Sparta in the eighth, seventh centuries for Greeks is an absolute model of how not to run a city.
sentences.zh: 在公元前八、七世纪，对于希腊人来说，斯巴达是“如何不该治理城市”的绝对典范。

sentences.en: It's terrible.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: The rich persecute the poor.
sentences.zh: 富人迫害穷人。

sentences.en: Everyone's kind of given over to all kinds of depravity.
sentences.zh: 每个人都沉溺于各种堕落之中。

sentences.en: They go to war with their neighbors over on the other side of Mount Tegatus, a place called Messenia, which is even a kind of richer agricultural land than Sparta is.
sentences.zh: 他们为了泰格特斯山另一侧的邻居——一个叫做美西尼亚的地方——而与他们开战，那里的农业土地甚至比斯巴达还要富饶。

sentences.en: The Spartans conquer it.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人征服了它。

sentences.en: This money then enhances the class differences.
sentences.zh: 这些财富随后加剧了阶级差异。

sentences.en: The whole city seems to be falling to pieces.
sentences.zh: 整个城市似乎正在四分五裂。

sentences.en: They also need military manpower to keep the Messenians down.
sentences.zh: 他们还需要军事兵力来镇压美西尼亚人。

sentences.en: And so they institute a radical redrafting of their constitution,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对宪法进行了激进的重新起草，

sentences.en: which basically transforms it into a kind of slave state where all the Spartan citizens are conditioned and trained to fight as warriors.
sentences.zh: 基本上将其转变为一种奴隶制国家，所有的斯巴达公民都被塑造成并训练成像战士一样战斗。

sentences.en: And this makes them the most formidable fighting force in Greece.
sentences.zh: 这使他们成为希腊最强大的战斗力量。

sentences.en: Sparta is the largest city.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达是最大的城市。

sentences.en: It's the most proficient military power in Greece.
sentences.zh: 它是希腊最精锐的军事力量。

sentences.en: As such, it is able basically to bring most of the Peloponnese under its rule.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，它基本上能够将伯罗奔纳芝的大部分地区置于其统治之下。

sentences.en: It plays a leading role in the Persian Wars, famous defense at Thermopylae.
sentences.zh: 它在波斯战争中发挥了主导作用，例如在温泉关的著名防御战。

sentences.en: It wins the Battle of Plataea in 479, the year after Thermopylae, which sees the Persian invasion brought to an end.
sentences.zh: 它在温泉关之后的次年，即公元前479年赢得了普拉提亚战役，宣告了波斯入侵的结束。

sentences.en: The rising power of Athens brings it to conflict with Sparta.
sentences.zh: 雅典实力的崛起使其与斯巴达发生冲突。

sentences.en: Sparta ends up winning that for a few years.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达最终赢得了那场战争并持续了几年。

sentences.en: It's kind of mastery of Greece is undisputed.
sentences.zh: 它对希腊的统治地位毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: But Greece being Greece, they're endlessly fighting with another.
sentences.zh: 但希腊毕竟是希腊，他们无休止地内讧。

sentences.en: The whole thing implodes.
sentences.zh: 整个体系崩溃了。

sentences.en: Thebes, a city that previously had been very, very marginal, very much looked down upon, rises to this incredible military peak and destroys Sparta in two famous battles.
sentences.zh: 底比斯，一个此前一直非常边缘化、备受瞧不起的城市，崛起达到了不可思议的军事巅峰，并在两场著名的战役中摧毁了斯巴达。

sentences.en: And from that point, and what the Thebans do is to divest the Spartans of Messenia, which up till then had basically provided them with their great power status.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，底比斯人做的事就是剥夺斯巴达对美西尼亚的控制权，直到那时，美西尼亚基本上一直是他们大国地位的支柱。

sentences.en: And once Messenia has gone, Sparta is immediately transformed into a kind of second class power.
sentences.zh: 一旦美西尼亚失去，斯巴达立即沦为一个二流强国。

sentences.en: From that point on, they obdurately cling to their independence, but they become more and more marginal and they end up absorbed into the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们顽固地坚守独立，但变得越来越边缘化，最终被并入罗马帝国。

sentences.en: And essentially, they become a kind of cosplay version of their ancestors.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们成了自己祖先的“角色扮演”版。

sentences.en: They, you know, they lay on kind of spectacular whipping demonstrations for the entertainment of visiting tourists and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们为了招待来访游客的娱乐目的，上演了壮观的鞭笞表演之类的东西。

sentences.en: When the Roman Empire falls, Sparta gets caught up in the process of barbarian invasion.
sentences.zh: 当罗马帝国灭亡时，斯巴达卷入了蛮族入侵的浪潮中。

sentences.en: It gets sacked.
sentences.zh: 它被洗劫了。

sentences.en: In the sixth century, Slavs invade, Sparta gets completely denuded.
sentences.zh: 在六世纪，斯拉夫人入侵，斯巴达彻底荒废。

sentences.en: People take to the mountains and the hills.
sentences.zh: 人们逃往山峦和丘陵。

sentences.en: And Mistras, which you, the Byzantine city that you referred to, basically, it's made of what remains of the urban fabric of Sparta.
sentences.zh: 米斯特拉斯，也就是你提到的拜占庭城市，基本上就是由斯巴达残存的城市建筑废墟构成的。

sentences.en: And no one lives in the Eurotus from that point up until the Greek War of Independence, when Sparta is refounded, you know,
sentences.zh: 从那时起直到希腊独立战争期间，埃夫罗塔斯河畔再无一人居住，当时斯巴达被重新建立，你知道的，

sentences.en: in this kind of classicizing way that the Greeks have after they've won their independence.
sentences.zh: 采用的是希腊人在赢得独立后惯用的那种复古经典方式。

sentences.en: And the myth is much greater than the reality of downtown Sparta today.
sentences.zh: 神话远比今天斯巴达市中心的现实要宏大得多。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But in a sense, that's always been the case.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，情况一直如此。

sentences.en: So how much?
sentences.zh: 所以究竟有多少？

sentences.en: It's always been a vital compliment to even at its absolute heyday.
sentences.zh: 即使在其鼎盛时期，这也一直是至关重要的补充。

sentences.en: When people came up against Sparta, they were fighting the myth as well as the reality.
sentences.zh: 当人们与斯巴达对抗时，他们对抗的既是现实，也是神话。

sentences.en: OK, let's get back to Kieran Roach's question then.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们回到基兰·罗奇的问题上来。

sentences.en: So everything we're going to be talking about in the rest of this podcast, how much is it, do you think, as far as anyone can say about ancient history,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们这个播客接下来的内容中要讨论的一切，就古代历史而言，

sentences.en: how much is it based on genuine historical evidence?
sentences.zh: 它究竟有多少是基于真实的实锤历史证据？

sentences.en: And how much is it a projection, as Kieran says, of other people's prejudices and other people's kind of wish fulfillment, in a way, about the Spartans?
sentences.zh: 又有多少正如基兰所说，是其他人偏见的投射，是人们对斯巴达的一种愿望实现？

sentences.en: So academic studies of Sparta are really tough because it's all about fragments of pottery, fragments of source material,
sentences.zh: 所以对斯巴达的学术研究真的很难，因为全都是陶器碎片、史料残片，

sentences.en: the sifting and the balancing of texts that might often be written kind of centuries apart.
sentences.zh: 对那些可能相隔几个世纪撰写的文本进行筛选和权衡。

sentences.en: So it is a challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个挑战。

sentences.en: And it's undoubtedly the case that an awful lot of what we know about Sparta, people who were consciously mythologizing it, whether because they admired it,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们对斯巴达的大量了解，都来自于那些有意识地将其神话化的人，无论是出于对它的崇拜，

sentences.en: which lots of people did, or whether because they hated it, which equally lots of people did.
sentences.zh: 就像许多人做的那样，还是出于对它的憎恨，同样有许多人这样做。

sentences.en: So I think it's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这非常困难。

sentences.en: But I think it's entirely justified to kind of construct a kind of sense of what the society had been like, because it's been so influential.
sentences.zh: 但我认为构建一种对这个社会曾经样子的认知是完全正当的，因为它实在太有影响力了。

sentences.en: It was massively influential on the Greeks back in antiquity, and it's been hugely influential in the modern period as well.
sentences.zh: 它在古代对希腊人产生了巨大影响，在现代时期也同样影响深远。

sentences.en: So I think you can kind of, you know, this isn't a kind of lecture for a degree course.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你可以，你知道的，这不像是学位课程的讲座。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: It's not the Open University.
sentences.zh: 这不是开放大学。

sentences.en: We don't want to go down that road.
sentences.zh: 我们不想走那条路。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: And we're not even Melvin Bragg.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至都不是梅尔文·布拉格。

sentences.en: I mean, no matter what some people may have said earlier in the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管某些人在本期播客早期可能说过什么。

sentences.en: As you said to me when we first discussed doing the podcast, it's all about the bants.
sentences.zh: 就像我们第一次讨论做这个播客时你对我说的那样，这全都是关于胡侃瞎聊。

sentences.en: It's all about the bants, yeah.
sentences.zh: 全都是胡侃瞎聊，对。

sentences.en: When my wife heard those words, she said, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 当我妻子听到这些话时，她说，别干了。

sentences.en: For God's sake, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 看在上帝的份上，别干了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's move on.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们继续。

sentences.en: So why is Sparta, Sparta, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么，斯巴达为什么会成为斯巴达，汤姆？

sentences.en: Is it about geography?
sentences.zh: 是因为地理原因吗？

sentences.en: geography?
sentences.zh: 地理原因？

sentences.en: Why has it become this military machine?
sentences.zh: 为什么它会变成这样一个军事机器？

sentences.en: Or is it less different from other Greek city-states than we commonly think?
sentences.zh: 还是说它并没有我们通常想象的那么不同于其他希腊城邦？

sentences.en: I think it's really different.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它真的很不一样。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, to begin with, it isn't different.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一开始，它其实并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: So back in the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 早在青铜时代。

sentences.en: So a further confusion is that it has two names.
sentences.zh: 另一个令人困惑的地方是它有两个名字。

sentences.en: It actually has loads of names.
sentences.zh: 其实它有好多名字。

sentences.en: So it's also called Lacedaemon.
sentences.zh: 所以它也被称为拉凯代梦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's what it's originally called.
sentences.zh: 这才是它最初的名字。

sentences.en: We know that because tablets have been found actually in Boatia and Thebes that names it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点，是因为在维奥蒂亚和底比斯出土的泥板上提到了这个名字。

sentences.en: It's mentioned in Homer.
sentences.zh: 荷马史诗中也有提及。

sentences.en: It's hollow Lacedaemon.
sentences.zh: 那是空洞的拉凯代梦。

sentences.en: Sparta seems to mean land that's sown.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达似乎意味着被播种的土地。

sentences.en: So Sparrow is I sow.
sentences.zh: 因为“斯帕罗”是我播种的意思。

sentences.en: So basically, Lacedaemon is the old name.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，拉凯代梦是旧称。

sentences.en: Sparta comes to mean this fertile valley where people are plowing and sowing.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达后来成了这个肥沃山谷的代名词，人们在那里犁地播种。

sentences.en: And I think that that's the key to Sparta's initial status is that it has this fertile valley and it is very well defended.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是斯巴达最初地位的关键所在，因为它拥有这个肥沃的山谷，而且防御极佳。

sentences.en: And the thing that makes Sparta aberrant is that they conquer their neighbours.
sentences.zh: 使斯巴达显得反常的是，他们征服了邻居。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they reduce them to a level of servitude that other Greeks regarded as shocking.
sentences.zh: 并将他们贬为其他希腊人视为令人震惊的奴役状态。

sentences.en: And the servitude is called helitage.
sentences.zh: 这种奴役制度被称为希洛特制度。

sentences.en: They're called helots.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为希洛特人。

sentences.en: We'll come to the helots in a sec.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就会谈到希洛特人。

sentences.en: But why does the military culture develop?
sentences.zh: 但军事文化是怎么发展起来的呢？

sentences.en: That's a question we've had tons of people asking that.
sentences.zh: 这个问题有无数人问过。

sentences.en: Ben Gladwin, for example, says, why does Sparta develop this unique military culture when there are so many different Greek city-states?
sentences.zh: 比如本·格拉德温说，为什么在有这么多不同希腊城邦的情况下，斯巴达会发展出这种独特的军事文化？

sentences.en: Why are they the outlier?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们是个特例？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, as ever with Greek history, there's a myth and then there's a probable reality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如希腊历史常有的那样，其中既有神话，也有可能的现实。

sentences.en: So the myth is that in the wake of the conquest of Mycenae, as I said, Sparta falls to pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以神话是，正如我所说，在征服迈锡尼之后，斯巴达分崩离析。

sentences.en: It becomes a model of bad order.
sentences.zh: 它成了失序的典范。

sentences.en: And an eminent Spartan by the name of Lycurgus, which means wolf worker, goes to Delphi and consults with the oracle.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫莱库古的杰出斯巴达人，意思是“狼工”，前往德尔斐并请教神谕。

sentences.en: And Apollo sees him and says, oh, I don't know who you are.
sentences.zh: 阿波罗看到他并说，哦，我不知道你是谁。

sentences.en: I'm not sure who you are.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定你是谁。

sentences.en: Lycurgus, are you a god or a man?
sentences.zh: 莱库古，你是神还是人？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: But I think you're probably a god.
sentences.zh: 但我猜你可能真的是个神。

sentences.en: So that's kind of, you know, this strange, ambivalent, heroic status that Lycurgus has.
sentences.zh: 所以吕库格斯拥有一种奇特的、矛盾的、具有英雄主义色彩的地位。

sentences.en: And the oracle gives Lycurgus a constitution, which basically provides, it transforms the citizens of Sparta into a military elite.
sentences.zh: 奥长官神谕赋予了吕库格斯一套宪法，这基本上将斯巴达公民转化为了一支军事精英阶层。

sentences.en: And they can do this because they've conquered Mycenae and so they can use the Mycenaeans as basically to grow the food.
sentences.zh: 他们能做到这一点是因为他们征服了迈锡尼，所以他们可以让迈锡尼人来帮他们种植粮食。

sentences.en: A slave, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是奴隶。

sentences.en: So Titaius, the poet, says that they're like donkeys laden down with heavy burdens.
sentences.zh: 因此，诗人泰台乌斯说他们就像负重累累的毛驴。

sentences.en: The Spartans also have people called perioikoi, which are people who live around Sparta, who can do the things like make the pots or make the armour or whatever.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人还有一种被称为“盘伊欧柯伊”的人，也就是住在斯巴达周边的人，他们负责做陶器、做盔甲之类的事情。

sentences.en: The Spartan warriors themselves, that's all they do.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达战士自己，他们唯一的职责就是打仗。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So any other Greek city, the people who fight, they do it on a strictly amateur basis.
sentences.zh: 所以，在任何其他的希腊城邦，参战的人都完全是业余性质的。

sentences.en: They're carpenters, they're whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们是木匠，干各种各样的活。

sentences.en: But in Sparta, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但在斯巴达，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: They are purely soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们纯粹是军人。

sentences.en: So a young Tom Holland is born in the year 450 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个年轻的汤姆·霍兰德出生于公元前450年左右。

sentences.en: How does his life work in Sparta?
sentences.zh: 他在斯巴达的生活是怎么样的呢？

sentences.en: So talk me through it.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲吧。

sentences.en: Well, young Tom Holland is born and he looks a bit wussy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，年轻的汤姆·霍兰德出生了，看起来有点娇弱。

sentences.en: So he'd probably, he'd be taken to these magistrates called ephors who were elected every year.
sentences.zh: 所以他大概会被带去见那些被称为监察官的官员，他们是每年选举产生的。

sentences.en: The ephors would inspect me.
sentences.zh: 监察官会检查我。

sentences.en: They would say, is he going to go up to be a mighty muscle-bound warrior?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，这小子以后能成为一个肌肉发达的勇士吗？

sentences.en: They'd probably say no.
sentences.zh: 他们大概会说不能。

sentences.en: I feel so sorry for you.
sentences.zh: 我真为你感到难过。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: And so I'd be taken to a place called the Apotheti, which is the dumping ground, which is a ravine at the foot of Mount Togatus.
sentences.zh: 所以我会被带到一个叫做“弃婴场”的地方，也就是一个垃圾场，那是托加图斯山脚下的一道沟壑。

sentences.en: And I'd be exposed there, along with all the other baby boys.
sentences.zh: 我会被和其他所有男婴一起抛弃在那里。

sentences.en: All the other Misfits.
sentences.zh: 所有这些格格不入的弃儿。

sentences.en: Don't pass muster.
sentences.zh: 不符合标准。

sentences.en: But let's say it's young Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 但假设那是年轻的多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: Wow, very different story.
sentences.zh: 哇，那完全是另一个故事了。

sentences.en: A fine, strapping young lad.
sentences.zh: 一个身体健壮、朝气蓬勃的年轻人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Clearly made to grow up and defend his city.
sentences.zh: 显然天生就是要长大并保卫他的城市。

sentences.en: Then at the age of seven, you'd go to the equivalent of a boarding school.
sentences.zh: 然后到了七岁，你就要去相当于寄宿学校的地方。

sentences.en: You'd go to a kind of barracks and you'd undergo what's called the agogae, which is, it's a kind of training procedure.
sentences.zh: 你会进入一种军营，并经历被称为“阿戈盖”的制度，这是一种训练程序。

sentences.en: And you'd be under, I mean, basically, your instructor would, in Greek, means a kind of a child herd.
sentences.zh: 而且你会受到——我的意思是，基本上，你的教官在希腊语里的意思就是某种放羊娃。

sentences.en: So you're being raised like animals.
sentences.zh: 所以你们是被当成动物一样养大的。

sentences.en: And it's that thing with Lycurgus, you know, the maker of wolves.
sentences.zh: 就像关于吕库格斯的那种说法，你知道的，狼的缔造者。

sentences.en: You're being, you're simultaneously being trained to be ferocious like a wolf, but also to be broken to control and discipline.
sentences.zh: 你们一方面被训练得像狼一样凶猛，但同时也要被驯服，接受控制和纪律约束。

sentences.en: So this is not Greyfriars in the Billy Bunter era?
sentences.zh: 所以这可不是比利·邦特时代格雷弗赖尔斯公学那种地方？

sentences.en: This is not.
sentences.zh: 这可不是。

sentences.en: No, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不，完全不是。

sentences.en: And so you are, you are schooled in the use of arMs.
sentences.zh: 所以你们接受了武器使用的训练。

sentences.en: You're schooled in drill.
sentences.zh: 你们接受了列队操练的训练。

sentences.en: You're schooled in wrestling.
sentences.zh: 你们接受了摔跤训练。

sentences.en: You're schooled to forage.
sentences.zh: 你们接受了野外觅食的训练。

sentences.en: So there'll be times where you were not fed enough.
sentences.zh: 所以会有吃不饱的时候。

sentences.en: So is this the chief?
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是那个头儿吗？

sentences.en: You have to go out.
sentences.zh: 你必须出去。

sentences.en: Is this the...
sentences.zh: 这就是那个……

sentences.en: No, that's it.
sentences.zh: 不，就是这样。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That's different because that's a game.
sentences.zh: 这不一样，因为那是个游戏。

sentences.en: This is, you know, you have to go out into the, onto the mountainside and kind of kill animals or you have to steal things from other people or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而这个，你知道的，你必须走到荒野里，走到山坡上去捕杀动物，或者你必须从别人那里偷东西之类的。

sentences.en: So there's a famous story of the, a boy who is found and he's got a fox, which he's going to eat.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个著名的故事，讲的是一个男孩被发现时，他藏了一只准备吃掉的狐狸。

sentences.en: And he hides it under his tunic and an elder stops him and asks him what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 他把它藏在束腰外衣下面，一个长辈拦住他，问他在干什么。

sentences.en: And he says absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 他说什么也没干。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the fox is gnawing away at his stomach.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，狐狸正在撕咬他的胃。

sentences.en: And the boy suddenly drops down dead and he hasn't mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 然后这个男孩突然倒地身亡，而他一直没提这事。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I mean, this, this story is clearly not true because who would eat a fox?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个故事显然不是真的，因为谁会去吃狐狸？

sentences.en: But it suggests that boys, you know, young boys are taking on vulpine characteristics.
sentences.zh: 但这表明孩子们，你知道的，这些年轻男孩正在染上狐狸般的特征。

sentences.en: They're trained to become foxes.
sentences.zh: 他们被训练得像狐狸一样。

sentences.en: But, and also that's kind of stoicism is, is absolutely key to the Spartan sense of themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且，这种坚忍不拔的精神绝对是斯巴达人自我认知至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, so, so the reed Sparta and the area around it, it's called Laconia.
sentences.zh: 所以，斯巴达及其周边地区被称为拉科尼亚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we still have the word laconic.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还保留着“简练”这个词（源自拉科尼亚）。

sentences.en: You're beaten.
sentences.zh: 你挨揍了。

sentences.en: If you talk too much, you're encouraged to say things as, as concisely as you possibly can.
sentences.zh: 如果你废话太多，就会被鼓励尽可能简明扼要地表达。

sentences.en: Just like you on this podcast, right?
sentences.zh: 就像你在播客里一样，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, exactly like me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直跟我一模一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the thing that's, the thing that's also very distinctive about Sparta is it's not just boys who get an education, girls do as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，斯巴达非常独特的地方在于，不仅仅是男孩能接受教育，女孩也可以。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We have tons of questions about girls and women.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多关于女孩和妇女的问题。

sentences.en: So, so girls also, you know, they're, they seem to be, have been taught to read, to write.
sentences.zh: 所以，女孩们也，你知道的，她们似乎被教导要识字、写字。

sentences.en: They're taught to be kind of forthright to, to express their opinions.
sentences.zh: 她们被教导要直言不讳、表达自己的观点。

sentences.en: They, they, they, they have this kind of distinctive dance where they slap their buttocks with the bottom of their feet.
sentences.zh: 她们有一种独特的舞蹈，用脚后跟拍打自己的屁股。

sentences.en: With the bottom of their feet?
sentences.zh: 用脚后跟拍打？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you kind of, you know, you sort of leap up, you leap up, you kick your legs up and you hit your buttocks with the, with the bottom of your feet.
sentences.zh: 所以你得，你知道的，你得跳起来，向上跳，把腿踢高，用脚后跟去踢自己的屁股。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So no one was doing that when I was in Sparta, disappointing.
sentences.zh: 我在斯巴达的时候可没人这么干，真让人失望。

sentences.en: Something they could, they could revive.
sentences.zh: 这是她们可以重新恢复的一项活动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They, they're, they're known as, they wear these kind of very skimpy slits, tunics that causes a lot of kind of prurient disapproval from, from Arthur Greek.
sentences.zh: 她们以穿着非常暴露、有开衩的束腰外衣而闻名，这引发了其他希腊人很多色情意味的非议。

sentences.en: Sometimes they wrestle naked.
sentences.zh: 有时她们会赤身裸体地摔跤。

sentences.en: And one of the things that girls do is, I mean, it's so, it's kind of every school boy's worst nightmare.
sentences.zh: 女孩们做的一件事是——我的意思是，这简直是每个男校学生的终极噩梦。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 说下去。

sentences.en: Is it that you, at certain points you, you, you have to strip naked and stand before all the girls?
sentences.zh: 就是你在某些时刻必须脱光衣服，站在所有女孩面前？

sentences.en: Oh God.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: And the girl, you know, if, if you don't measure up, the girls are encouraged to laugh and mock you.
sentences.zh: 而且女孩们，你知道的，如果你不达标，女孩们就会被鼓励对你嘲笑和讥讽。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that's fun.
sentences.zh: 听起来挺好玩的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then, I mean, it's good for the soul.
sentences.zh: 而且，这有益于净化灵魂。

sentences.en: So at a certain point you, you will play the cheese game that we talked about.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个阶段，你会玩我们刚才提到的奶酪游戏。

sentences.en: And then the, the, the odd thing is so that, that the ideal is simultaneously to, to kind of encourage this egalitarianism, but it doesn't mean that everyone's equal.
sentences.zh: 然后，奇怪的事情在于，他们的理想是同时鼓励这种平均主义，但这并不意味着每个人都是平等的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's this ferocious sense of, of competition.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种极其激烈的竞争意识。

sentences.en: You have to make yourself the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你必须让自己成为最优秀的。

sentences.en: And if you win the cheese game or if you pass kind of various tests, then the, your huge opportunity is that you, you can join the cryptea, this kind of elite.
sentences.zh: 如果你赢了奶酪游戏，或者如果你通过了各种测试，那么你将获得的巨大机遇就是你可以加入克里普提亚，这个精英组织。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which is basically Duke of Edinburgh award, the gold, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是爱丁堡公爵奖的黄金级别，不管它叫什么。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Gold award.
sentences.zh: 金奖。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Gold award.
sentences.zh: 金奖。

sentences.en: And you go up into the mountains, you go down the other side, you go into Mycenae and you have to kill a helot.
sentences.zh: 然后你走到群山之中，翻过山的另一边，进入迈锡尼，你必须杀死一个黑劳士。

sentences.en: So a helot is a slave.
sentences.zh: 所以黑劳士就是奴隶。

sentences.en: These are the people who are tilling the land.
sentences.zh: 这些人是耕种土地的人。

sentences.en: These are the Mycenaeans.
sentences.zh: 这些就是迈锡尼人。

sentences.en: And if you do that, then you come back and you get your gold award and you have the chance
sentences.zh: 如果你做到了这一点，你回来就能拿到你的金奖，并且有机会

sentences.en: to enter what's called the Hippaeus, which is basically the cavalry, the knights, but this being Sparta, they're not, they're all on foot.
sentences.zh: 进入被称为“希帕伊斯”的组织，这基本上就是骑兵、骑士，但既然这里是斯巴达，他们其实全都是步兵。

sentences.en: But these are the 300 who go with Lenny Dust of Thermopylae, the famous 300 as in the film.
sentences.zh: 但这就是跟随列奥尼达前往温泉关的那三百勇士，也就是电影里的那著名三百人。

sentences.en: And talk to me about the killing the slave.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲杀死奴隶的事。

sentences.en: You can kill any slave.
sentences.zh: 你可以杀死任何奴隶。

sentences.en: You can just leap on them and stab them in the neck or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接扑上去往他脖子上捅一刀之类的。

sentences.en: So, so helots are, again, very, a very distinctive kind of phenomenon in Sparta.
sentences.zh: 所以，黑劳士在斯巴达再次是一个非常独特的现象。

sentences.en: So, you know, people kind of discuss what were helots.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们总在讨论黑劳士到底是什么。

sentences.en: Basically helots were helots.
sentences.zh: 基本上黑劳士就是黑劳士。

sentences.en: They were, they were distinctive.
sentences.zh: 他们非常与众不同。

sentences.en: There was a, there was a village in, in Laconia called Helos.
sentences.zh: 拉科尼亚有一个村庄叫黑洛斯。

sentences.en: And so there were all kinds of stories that these were the first helots.
sentences.zh: 因此有各种各样的传说称这些人就是最早的黑劳士。

sentences.en: Other stories were that the first helots were Spartans who'd been cowards and had been reduced to this servitude to humiliate them.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的传说说最早的黑劳士是那些曾表现怯懦并被降为这种奴役状态以羞辱他们的斯巴达人。

sentences.en: But basically helots are there to work the land and to provide the messes that enable the Spartan warriors to function as warriors.
sentences.zh: 但基本上黑劳士的存在就是为了耕种土地，并提供维持斯巴达战士作为战士日常运作的集体伙食。

sentences.en: And so it's, it's a kind of chicken and egg situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种先有鸡还是先有蛋的情况。

sentences.en: What comes first?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么先生的？

sentences.en: Is it the militarism of Sparta that enables them to keep the helots down?
sentences.zh: 是斯巴达的军国主义使他们能够镇压黑劳士吗？

sentences.en: Or do they have to keep the helots down?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们必须镇压黑劳士？

sentences.en: Because otherwise the helots will rise up and kill them.
sentences.zh: 因为否则黑劳士就会起义并杀死他们。

sentences.en: We had a question about this.
sentences.zh: 我们之前就收到过关于这个的问题。

sentences.en: We had lots of questions.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多问题。

sentences.en: Benji, why didn't the helots revolt?
sentences.zh: 本吉问，为什么黑劳士不反抗？

sentences.en: And were the Spartans afraid of it?
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人害怕这个吗？

sentences.en: And Paul Hogarth says, how, how paranoid were the Spartans of a helot uprising?
sentences.zh: 保罗·霍加斯问，斯巴达人对黑劳士起义的偏执程度达到了什么地步？

sentences.en: And does that explain their militarism?
sentences.zh: 这能解释他们的军国主义吗？

sentences.en: So was there ever a helot uprising?
sentences.zh: 那么，历史上真的发生过黑劳士起义吗？

sentences.en: Well, the Spartans are very paranoid about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，斯巴达人对此非常偏执。

sentences.en: I mean, I think a lot of the, you know, for a free citizen to be whipped or to be beaten as Spartans were, you know, it's kind of humiliating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为很多，你知道的，对于一个自由公民来说，被鞭打或殴打——正如斯巴达人所经历的那样——这是一种羞辱。

sentences.en: And so there's this paradox that, that nowhere in Greece are people more free than in Sparta.
sentences.zh: 所以存在这样一个悖论：希腊没有任何地方的人比斯巴达人更自由。

sentences.en: Nowhere are they more like slaves.
sentences.zh: 但也没有任何地方的人比他们更像奴隶。

sentences.en: And I think kind of hanging over it is a reminder of what will happen to them if the helots gain power and conquer them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中一直笼罩着一种阴影，提醒着他们如果黑劳士夺取权力并征服了他们，他们将会遭遇什么。

sentences.en: The Spartans, every year the Ephors declare war against the Mycenaeans, which they see as licensing the murder of helots.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人每年都会由监察官向迈锡尼人宣战，他们认为这等于是为谋杀黑劳士发放了合法执照。

sentences.en: So Herodotus has this kind of very chilling phrase where he says that the Spartans alone do not regard murder as a crime.
sentences.zh: 所以希罗多德有一句非常令人不寒而栗的话，他说只有斯巴达人不把谋杀视为犯罪。

sentences.en: And they are, they practice a kind of very self-conscious eugenics.
sentences.zh: 而且他们实行一种非常具有自我意识的优生学。

sentences.en: So just as they, you know, they, they breed themselves, they're, they're famous for breeding horses, for breeding dogs and for breeding themselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如他们培育自己一样——他们以培育马匹、培育狗以及培育自身而闻名。

sentences.en: So this is why they, they chuck out people who, you know, babies that don't measure up.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们会抛弃那些不符合标准的婴儿。

sentences.en: So conversely, the, the members of the Cryptaea, when they're passing their Duke of Edinburgh, they're given people to, they're given helots to kill.
sentences.zh: 因此反过来看，克里普提亚的成员们在通过他们的爱丁堡公爵奖时，会被分配人去杀——会被分配黑劳士去杀。

sentences.en: And these helots are the ones who've shown initiative, who, who are smarter or clever or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而这些黑劳士正是那些表现出进取心、更聪明、更机智或诸如此类特质的人。

sentences.en: So they're trying to breed an adultish, servile population.
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图繁育出一个带点成年人气息、奴性十足的人口群体。

sentences.en: So they've actually singled out the brightest, most, most talented helots, Mycenaeans.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们实际上挑出了最聪明、最有才华的黑劳士，也就是迈锡尼人。

sentences.en: And they basically say to their own children, teenagers, I guess, go and kill them.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上对自己的孩子——我想大概是十几岁的青少年——说，去把他们杀掉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's then the mark of, you know, that you've, you've kind of passed the grade.
sentences.zh: 而这随后就成了你通过了某种考验的标志。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what they also do is for entertainment, sometimes when they're in their messes, they will, they will bring a helot in and the helots are made to wear these kind of revolting.
sentences.zh: 他们还会做的一件事是为了娱乐，有时当他们在食堂聚餐时，他们会把一个黑劳士带进来，而黑劳士们被迫穿着那种令人作呕的衣服。

sentences.en: They're making dog skins, you know, it's designed to make them look ridiculous and ugly and scabby.
sentences.zh: 他们用狗皮制作，你知道的，这旨在让他们看起来荒谬、丑陋且满身疥疮。

sentences.en: And they will get the helots drunk on unmixed wine.
sentences.zh: 他们会让黑劳士们喝纯酒喝到大醉。

sentences.en: So the Greeks mix wine.
sentences.zh: 所以希腊人平时是把酒兑着喝的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: With water.
sentences.zh: 兑水。

sentences.en: They give it, they give it neat.
sentences.zh: 他们给黑劳士喝的是不兑水的原酒。

sentences.en: And the helot gets absolutely off his face.
sentences.zh: 然后那个黑劳士就彻底神志不清了。

sentences.en: He kind of collapses in a drunken stupor.
sentences.zh: 他会在醉酒的昏迷中瘫倒下去。

sentences.en: However, the Spartans then kind of ran the evening off by pelting him with animal bones.
sentences.zh: 然而，斯巴达人随后会通过用动物骨头砸他来结束当晚的活动。

sentences.en: And the whole thing is designed both to, you know, addict helots to drink.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的设计，既是为了让黑劳士对酒精上瘾——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 比如，比方说美国南部。

sentences.zh: 这里面哪怕有一点点这种成分吗？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 完全没有，没有，没有。

sentences.zh: 因为对希腊人来说，令人震惊的是黑劳士其实是希腊人。

sentences.en: So, and actually more than that, they, they're Dorian.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们实际上是多利安人。

sentences.en: So this is also an important part of how the Spartans see themselves, is that they see themselves as these invaders called Dorians,
sentences.zh: 所以这也是斯巴达人如何看待自己的一个重要部分，他们认为自己是被称为多利安人的入侵者，

sentences.en: who have, have swept southwards and conquered the Peloponnese with these kind of great Achaean cities, Mycenae and Argos, and of course, Sparta.
sentences.zh: 这些入侵者向南席卷，征服了伯罗奔尼撒半岛，以及迈锡尼、阿尔戈斯等伟大的亚该亚城市，当然还有斯巴达。

sentences.en: And the Mycenaeans are Dorians, like the Spartans.
sentences.zh: 迈锡尼人也是多利安人，就像斯巴达人一样。

sentences.en: So in that sense, they're kin.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，他们是同胞。

sentences.en: And so actually the humiliations that are imposed on them, the determination to breed them into a kind of slave people,
sentences.zh: 因此，强加在他们身上的羞辱，以及决心将他们繁育成某种奴隶民族的意志，

sentences.en: isn't because they are seen as, as alien, isn't because of, of racism.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们被视为异类，也不是因为种族主义。

sentences.en: It's absolutely the opposite.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's because there is this incredible sense of kinship.
sentences.zh: 这是因为存在着一种不可思议的血缘感。

sentences.en: But Tom, in that case, here's my, here's an obvious question.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，既然如此，我这里有一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.zh: 究竟是什么让一个斯巴达人成为斯巴达人？

sentences.en: So how do you become a Spartan if they're, if they're the same, if they're kind of vaguely related to the other Dorian peoples, to the Mycenaeans?
sentences.zh: 如果他们是一样的，如果他们和其他多利安人、和迈锡尼人有着某种模糊的亲缘关系，那你究竟是怎么成为斯巴达人的？

sentences.en: Why, how are the Spartans Spartans?
sentences.zh: 为什么、斯巴达人究竟是怎么成为斯巴达人的？

sentences.en: Is it just particular families?
sentences.zh: 难道只是取决于特定的家族吗？

sentences.en: Is it literally the fact of residency in, in Sparta?
sentences.zh: 难道真的是因为住在斯巴达这个事实吗？

sentences.en: What is it that makes you Spartan?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么让你成为斯巴达人？

sentences.en: You have to, you have to be the son of freeborn Spartan parents.
sentences.zh: 你必须是自由出生的斯巴达父母的儿子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you have to have a certain kind of land qualification.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须拥有某种土地资格。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And this is, this is seen as the kind of the radical innovation of the Lycurgian revolution.
sentences.zh: 这被视为吕库古革命的一种根本性变革。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's why Sparta has appealed to the left as well as to the right, is that these incredible social differences, which had seen the rich oppressing the poor,
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么斯巴达既吸引了左翼也吸引了右翼的原因，因为那些曾导致富人压迫穷人的不可思议的社会差异，

sentences.en: kind of get dissolved.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上被瓦解了。

sentences.en: And everybody has to live the same life.
sentences.zh: 每个人都必须过同样的生活。

sentences.en: They all have to belong to a barracks.
sentences.zh: 他们都必须属于一个军营。

sentences.en: They all have to eat the same food.
sentences.zh: 他们都必须吃同样的食物。

sentences.en: They all have to dress in the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们都必须以同样的方式着装。

sentences.en: They all have to fight in the same battle line.
sentences.zh: 他们都必须在同一个战斗方阵中作战。

sentences.en: And the reality is, of course, that there are still people who are considerably richer than other people, but there has to be a certain property qualification.
sentences.zh: 但现实当然是，仍然有些人比其他人要富裕得多，不过你必须达到一定的财产资格标准。

sentences.en: Now, the effect of this over time is that, you know, Spartan warriors die.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这样做的结果是，你知道的，斯巴达战士会战死。

sentences.en: There is a kind of, you know, as is always the way the rich do tend to kind of increasingly monopolize land.
sentences.zh: 正如常有的情况一样，富人往往倾向于越来越多地垄断土地。

sentences.en: And so there's a steady kind of collapse in the number of people who are qualified to serve as Spartans.
sentences.zh: 因此，有资格成为斯巴达人的人数在稳步下降。

sentences.en: And that's one of the reasons that ultimately leads to the collapse of Spartan power.
sentences.zh: 这也是最终导致斯巴达权势崩溃的原因之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: So this, again, goes right the way back to the beginnings, is that most of the Spartans are Dorian, as I said, but there are families that aren't.
sentences.zh: 所以，这同样要追溯到最初的起源，正如我所说，大多数斯巴达人是多利安人，但也有一些家族并非如此。

sentences.en: And two of these families are, provide the two kings that rule at any one time.
sentences.zh: 其中两个家族提供了任何特定时期统治这里的两位国王。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: So Sparta is very, Sparta is kind of a weird mix.
sentences.zh: 所以斯巴达非常——斯巴达是一种奇怪的混合体。

sentences.en: So you've got the efforts, the elected magistrates.
sentences.zh: 你有埃福尔（监察官），也就是选举产生的行政长官。

sentences.en: You've got the assembly, which is kind of public assembly.
sentences.zh: 你有公民大会，这是一种公共集会。

sentences.en: You've got the equivalent of a senate.
sentences.zh: 你拥有相当于参议院的机构。

sentences.en: Gerousia is literally the Greek for senate.
sentences.zh: 长老会议（Gerousia）在希腊语中字面意思就是参议院。

sentences.en: It's assembly of old men, which, again, has kind of consultative power.
sentences.zh: 它是老者议会，同样拥有某种咨询权力。

sentences.en: And then you have two kings.
sentences.zh: 然后你有两位国王。

sentences.en: And both of these kings are descended, ultimately, they say, from Heracles, the great kind of paradigmatic Greek hero, who's an Achaean.
sentences.zh: 这两位国王最终都宣称自己是赫拉克勒斯的后代，赫拉克勒斯是伟大的希腊典型英雄，而他是一位亚该亚人。

sentences.en: So, weirdly, the kings in Sparta are not Dorian.
sentences.zh: 所以，奇怪的是，斯巴达的国王并不是多利安人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They're Achaean.
sentences.zh: 他们是亚该亚人。

sentences.en: That is strange.
sentences.zh: 这真奇怪。

sentences.en: It's kind of linked with the vanished past, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，这大概与消逝的过去有关吧。

sentences.en: Yes, and basically, it means that, you know, we were talking about the Olympics and how Olympian, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上这意味着，我们之前在谈论奥运会以及奥运会如何让希腊人——

sentences.en: winners in the Olympics provide the Greeks with a reminder of the heroic age, the age of heroes, and how heroes don't necessarily have the meaning that they have for us.
sentences.zh: 奥运会的获胜者为希腊人提供了对英雄时代、英雄纪元的提醒，以及英雄对我们来说并不一定具有他们字面意义上的含义。

sentences.en: Heroes are often very sinister figures, dangerous figures who are kind of midway between humans and the gods.
sentences.zh: 英雄通常是非常阴险的人物、危险的人物，他们处于人类和神灵之间。

sentences.en: And the Spartans' kings have that role.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达的国王就扮演了这样的角色。

sentences.en: And so, there's all kinds of myths about why there are two kings.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于为什么会有两位国王，流传着各种各样的神话。

sentences.en: The most popular myth is that there's a Spartan king.
sentences.zh: 最流行的神话是一个斯巴达国王的故事。

sentences.en: He has twins.
sentences.zh: 他生了一对双胞胎。

sentences.en: The Spartans don't, he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后他死了，斯巴达人不知道该由谁来继承王位。

sentences.en: The Spartans don't know who should succeed.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去德尔斐求签。

sentences.en: So, they go to Delphi.
sentences.zh: 德尔斐说他们两个都应该统治，但年纪较大的那个应该作为长王，这真是一种经典的、毫无帮助的回答。

sentences.en: Delphi says they should both rule, but the one who's eldest should be senior, which is kind of classically unhelpful.
sentences.zh: 所以，德尔斐的解决方案是一只手给出了解决方法，另一只手又把它收了回去。

sentences.en: So, yeah, kind of Delphi's solution, you know, gives the solution with one hand and takes it away with the other.
sentences.zh: 于是斯巴达人说，好吧，没问题，那我们就让这两位国王都上位，但我们怎么才能知道谁是哥哥呢？

sentences.en: So, the Spartans say, fine, okay, so we'll have these two kings, but how are we going to find out who the elder one is?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有个迈锡尼人，一个黑劳士，建议说：

sentences.en: And so, a Mycenae, interestingly, a helot, suggests, well,
sentences.zh: 观察王后，看她先给他们中的哪一个洗澡，以此假设年纪较大的儿子会是她最偏爱的。

sentences.en: watch the queen and see which one of them she bathes first on the assumption that the elder son is going to be the favourite.
sentences.zh: 于是他们观察王后——其实她不是王后，斯巴达没有王后，而是国王的妻子。

sentences.en: And so, they watch the queen and they, she's not actually a queen, Sparta doesn't have queens, but the wife of the king.
sentences.zh: 他们看是哪一个孩子，那个孩子就成了资深王室分支的创立者，另一个则是初级分支。

sentences.en: And they see which one it is and that then becomes the founder of the senior branch of kings and the other one is the junior branch.
sentences.zh: 这种被称为双王制的制度一直延续到了我想是公元三世纪。

sentences.en: And that goes right the way through to, I think, the third century, this diarchy it's called.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常奇怪的体制。

sentences.en: That's a very strange system.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在进入茶歇之前，还有一个非常简短的问题。

sentences.zh: 黑汤是一道出了名的令人作呕的菜肴。

sentences.zh: 斯巴达人会带去生食材，由黑劳士厨师将它们炖煮出来。

sentences.en: So, a Spartan would bring the raw ingredients, the helot cooks would brew it up.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一种血汤。

sentences.zh: 斯巴达人会狼吞虎咽地吃下它。

sentences.zh: 任何来访者都会说这东西太恶心了。

sentences.zh: 你想给我讲讲克里昂米尼吗？

sentences.zh: 他是个扩张主义者...

sentences.en: And Herodotus, the first historian, is basically our main source, often our only source for early Sparta.
sentences.zh: 而希罗多德作为第一位历史学家，基本上是我们了解早期斯巴达的主要史料，通常也是唯一的史料来源。

sentences.en: And it's clear that Herodotus has spoken to lots of different people about Cleomenes because he gives quite different perspectives on him.
sentences.zh: 显然，希罗多德曾与许多不同的人谈论过克里昂米尼，因为他对克里昂米尼的看法有着相当大的不同。

sentences.en: But Cleomenes is a king who rules for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 但克里昂米尼是一位统治了很长时间的国王。

sentences.en: And that means that he's able to build up quite a power base.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他能够建立起相当雄厚的权力基础。

sentences.en: And he's a very, he's an unusually imaginative and expansionist king.
sentences.zh: 而且他是一个非常、极其富有想象力和扩张主义的国王。

sentences.en: Spartans, the tradition is that they are very hidebound.
sentences.zh: 传统上，斯巴达人总是显得非常保守顽固。

sentences.en: Cleomenes seems not to have been.
sentences.zh: 但克里昂米尼似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: He plays kind of key roles in various developments in the decades before the Persian invasions.
sentences.zh: 在波斯入侵前的几十年里，他在各种事态发展中扮演了某种关键角色。

sentences.en: So he, the Delphic Oracle starts telling Spartans, go and chuck the tyrants out of Athens.

sentences.en: So Cleomenes does that.
sentences.zh: 于是克里昂米尼就照做了。

sentences.en: But he then gets terribly upset when the Athenians decide they're going to set up a democracy.
sentences.zh: 但当雅典人决定建立民主制时，他气得要命。

sentences.zh: 于是他试图阻止他们。

sentences.zh: 所以，马修·希兹本特说，斯巴达、雅典、苏格兰、英格兰，彼此争吵时总是很高兴，总准备把对方打得落花流水，直到一个共同的敌人，波斯，

sentences.zh: 但在我看来——我不是在批评马修·希兹本特——但实际情况恰好相反，对吧？

sentences.en: That, that, that, that, that, the common defense comes before the Peloponnesian War, which is when they, when they, so the Peloponnesian War, um, Sparta wins that.
sentences.zh: 那就是，共同防御发生在伯罗奔尼撒战争之前，也就是他们，他们——所以伯罗奔尼撒战争，嗯，斯巴达赢了那场战争。

sentences.en: I mean, basically that ends Athens' period of glory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上那就结束了雅典的辉煌时期。

sentences.en: Um, why, why, why did the other Greek cities not side with Athens when Sparta is so,

sentences.en: is it because they're frightened of Sparta or is it because they are much more resentful and suspicious of Athens than sort of modern, you know, Athena files would, would imagine?
sentences.zh: 是因为他们害怕斯巴达，还是因为他们对雅典的怨恨和怀疑，远比现代那些，你知道的，雅典迷们想象的要深得多？

sentences.en: Well, uh, basically Athens overreaches itself, so it launches this completely, uh, abortive invasion of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，基本上是因为雅典自视过高、盲目冒进，所以才发起了这场完全是，呃，流产的对西西里的入侵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, so Alcibiades is, again, we talked about it in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，阿尔西比亚德斯——同样，我们在奥运会那一期聊过。

sentences.en: He won, he wins, you know, he wins the top three places in the chariot race.
sentences.zh: 他赢了，你知道的，他在战车比赛中包揽了前三名。

sentences.en: Um, he gets accused of, um, impiety in Athens, uh, and basically he's the guy behind the Sicilian invasion, but he has,

sentences.en: he ends up fleeing and he ends up in Sparta and he advises the Spartans on what to do.
sentences.zh: 他最后逃跑了，跑到了斯巴达，并向斯巴达人出谋划策。

sentences.en: The least, the things that the Athenians would least like.
sentences.zh: 专挑雅典人最不愿意看到的事情下手。

sentences.en: Um, and basically the Athenian war effort kind of crumbles away after that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上雅典的战争机器从那以后就有点崩溃了。

sentences.en: Um, and amazingly Sparta is able to cast itself as, as the defender of freedom, even though, um, it, it, it obviously isn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，神奇的是，斯巴达竟然能把自己包装成——包装成自由的捍卫者，尽管，嗯，它——它——它显然并不是。

sentences.en: And when the, uh, the, the walls of Athens are pulled down to pipes, um, people say this is the day for the beginning of freedom of Greece,
sentences.zh: 当，呃，雅典的城墙被拆毁到只剩管子时，嗯，人们说这是希腊自由开始的日子，

sentences.en: but it isn't because Sparta is a kind of brutal militarist power that, um, insists on having its own way that, um,
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此，因为斯巴达是一个残暴的军国主义强权，嗯，它坚持要按自己的意愿行事，嗯，

sentences.en: um, kind of, you know, it, it, it instinctively wants to subordinate almost everybody that it comes up againSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，某种程度上，你知道的，它——它——它本能地想要把几乎所有它遇到的对手都置于其统治之下。

sentences.en: Um, it, it can't reduce them to heritage, but it certainly wants to, to, to subordinate them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它——它可能没法把他们降为世袭奴隶，但它绝对想要——想要——想要让他们俯首称臣。

sentences.en: And so in the aftermath of the Peloponnesian war, its power just melts away.
sentences.zh: 所以在伯罗奔尼撒战争之后，它的力量直接烟消云散了。

sentences.en: And amazingly within, you know, just a few decades, the Athenians are back there, you know, they've got their fleet up, back up in working order.
sentences.zh: 神奇的是，在你知道的短短几十年内，雅典人又回来了，你知道的，他们的舰队重新恢复并正常运作了。

sentences.en: And you've got Thebes that, you know, the third of these great cities, which up till then had always been, I'd say the, the, the, the,
sentences.zh: 还有底比斯，你知道的，这三大城邦中的第三个，在那之前它一直都是，我想说，这——这——这——

sentences.en: the majority of Thebans sided with the Persians.
sentences.zh: 大多数底比斯人都站在波斯一边。

sentences.en: And that's something that the Spartans and the Athenians never let them forget.
sentences.zh: 这也是斯巴达人和雅典人永远不会忘记的一点。

sentences.en: But you, you have this, um, this general of absolute genius called Epaminondas, who radically recalibrates, um, military strategy and is able to defeat the Spartan war machine,
sentences.zh: 但是你，你有这样一位，嗯，具有绝对天才的将军，名叫伊巴密浓达，他彻底重新校准了，嗯，军事战略，并能够击败斯巴达的战争机器，

sentences.en: which up until that point had been invincible.
sentences.zh: 而在那之前，这台战争机器一直是不可战胜的。

sentences.en: And there, there is this great battle, um, at, at Lyotra in 371, where the myth of Spartan invincibility is, is completely shattered.
sentences.zh: 然后，在那里发生了一场大战，嗯，公元前371年的留克特拉战役，斯巴达不可战胜的神话被彻底粉碎了。

sentences.en: And the, the, the Spartans try and, um, and kind of reconstitute, um, uh, their army.
sentences.zh: 然后，斯巴达人试图，嗯，并且某种程度上重建了，嗯，他们的军队。

sentences.en: But again, they're kind of shattered, uh, at a place called Mantanera, actually in the Peloponnese, um, in 362.
sentences.zh: 但同样，他们在公元前362年一个叫做曼丁尼亚的地方——实际上在伯罗奔尼撒半岛——再次被打得粉碎。

sentences.en: And, and that essentially is it because, you know, as I said, the, the, the, the Thebans liberate the Mycenaeans.
sentences.zh: 然后，基本上就是这样了，因为，你知道的，就像我说的，底比斯人解放了迈锡尼人。

sentences.en: And from that point on, Sparta is, is a busted flush.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，斯巴达就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: Why didn't they do what the Romans did, which is basically crush all their neighbours, absorb them or whatever, and become a, and the momentum of military conquests,
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不去做罗马人做的事，也就是基本上粉碎所有邻国，吞并它们或诸如此类的，然后成为一个，并且军事征服的势头，

sentences.en: just carry them from victory to victory.
sentences.zh: 直接把他们从一场胜利推向另一场胜利？

sentences.en: Why didn't Sparta manage to do that?
sentences.zh: 为什么斯巴达做不到这一点？

sentences.en: Because the whole basis of the Lycurgon constitution is that you have a Spartan elite sitting atop a volcano.
sentences.zh: 因为莱库古宪法的整个基础就是，你让一个斯巴达精英阶层坐在火山口上。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: And the Spartans are incredibly conservative and they're incredibly proud of this constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且斯巴达人极其保守，他们对这部宪法感到无上的骄傲。

sentences.en: And so they refuse to change it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拒绝改变它。

sentences.en: And the strange thing is, is that, you know, all the way, all the way through the centuries that lead up to the, the, the absorption of Sparta into the Roman empire, they,
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，你知道的，在通往斯巴达被并入罗马帝国的这漫长岁月里，他们——

sentences.en: they assume that the answer to their problems is to go back to this Lycurgon constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们以为解决问题的方法就是回到这部莱库古宪法上去。

sentences.en: So you have repeated attempts to try and reanimate it and, and people want to believe in it.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有反复的尝试来试图让它复活，而且人们愿意相信这一点。

sentences.en: So Cicero says of the, of the Spartans that they're the only people in the world who have lived, you know, with customs and, um, laws that have been unchanged for 700 years.
sentences.zh: 所以西塞罗谈到斯巴达人时说，他们是世界上唯一一个凭借延续了700年不变的风俗和，嗯，法律生活的人。

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't true, but the Spartans are able to kind of convince the Romans that this is the case and people want to believe it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是真的，但斯巴达人能够让罗马人相信事实确实如此，而且人们也愿意相信。

sentences.en: And actually the idea that, that Sparta is unchanging is a crucial part of, you know, of this idea of it as a mirage.
sentences.zh: 事实上，斯巴达是不变的这一观念，是这种海市蜃楼观念的一个至关重要的部分。

sentences.en: It's a crucial part of both what the Spartans want to believe and therefore what outsiders want to believe.
sentences.zh: 这是斯巴达人想要相信的，以及因此局外人想要相信的，这两者的一个至关重要的部分。

sentences.zh: 嗯，《星期日泰晤士报》的撰稿人乔希·格兰西问我们，把斯巴达人描述为法西斯或准法西斯，在任何方面是准确的还是具有历史相关性的？

sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多问题。

sentences.zh: 所以我们收到了一些关于维多利亚时代英国的问题，例如，斯巴达美德、阿诺德校长、拉格鲁公学以及公学传统。
